Recommendation: Split into 6-7 child requirements, one per article (with exclusion vs. selection criteria kept distinct), each independently sized and INVEST-evaluated at the story level.
- Testable: No conformance test suite, sample instance documents, or codelist validation mechanism is referenced. No specification of edge-case handling for national transpositions that add criteria beyond Directive minimums. Legal test oracle is ambiguous (2004/18/EC literal text vs. mapping to 2014/24/EU), and the conformance tier (closed vs. extensible schema) is undefined — these gaps hold regardless of historical vs. current framing. Recommendation: Define an explicit test oracle and conformance tier (additive-only vs. strictly closed schema) per split child requirement; provide sample instance documents and codelist validation; use lightweight Given/When/Then or Gherkin-style acceptance criteria scaffolding as an interim improvement.

original_text: National requirements for qualitative selection and exclusion MUST correspond to the EC criteria given in Article 45-50.
refined_text:
PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_002a: National exclusion grounds for economic operators MUST correspond to the mandatory and discretionary exclusion grounds defined in Directive 2014/24/EU, Article 57 (assumed as the correct current legal basis, replacing the repealed Directive 2004/18/EC Article 45 reference). Correspondence is verified by a documented crosswalk mapping each national exclusion ground to its matching Article 57 paragraph, signed off by a legal/procurement SME, and validated against the applicable ESPD exclusion-grounds data fields with zero unmapped or conflicting entries.

PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_002b: National qualitative selection criteria for suitability to pursue a professional activity, economic/financial standing, and technical/professional ability MUST correspond to Directive 2014/24/EU, Articles 58-60 (assumed as the correct current legal basis, replacing the repealed Directive 2004/18/EC Articles 46-48 reference). Correspondence is verified by a documented crosswalk mapping each national criterion to its matching article and paragraph, signed off by a legal/procurement SME, and validated against the applicable ESPD selection-criteria data fields with zero unmapped or conflicting entries.

PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_002c: Before the crosswalks in PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_002a and PEPPOL_APPROVED_REQ_002b are approved, the legal citation basis MUST be formally confirmed by Legal/SME review within 10 business days (assumed) of this requirement's approval, explicitly determining whether Directive 2014/24/EU Articles 57-64 (assumed) or a specific national transposition instrument is the authoritative reference, and this determination MUST be recorded as a dated, versioned legal-reference document before any downstream ESPD field-mapping or exclusion-ground data model work begins.
findings_used:
- Independent: The requirement anchors to 'Article 45-50' without specifying a directive, version, or date. Cross-checking content confirms this article range matches the repealed Directive 2004/18/EC (Art. 45 exclusion, 46 suitability, 47 financial standing, 48 technical ability), not the current Directive 2014/24/EU (which places this content in Art. 57-64). This is a Blocker-severity legal-currency risk, not merely a documentation nicety. Additionally, as a root/policy-tier item, downstream requirements (ESPD field definitions, exclusion-ground data models) likely depend on this item rather than vice versa, which is expected at this tier but still means standalone independence cannot be confirmed until the citation and hierarchy position are resolved. Recommendation: BLOCKER: Engage Legal/SME immediately to confirm whether 'Article 45-50' is a stale reference to repealed Directive 2004/18/EC or reflects an intentional PEPPOL-internal/national numbering rationale. If stale, raise an urgent remediation ticket to remap to Directive 2014/24/EU Art. 57-64 or the current national transposition before any further backlog action. Separately, pin the exact legal source (directive, version, date) once confirmed, and document this item's position in the requirement hierarchy (policy-tier parent vs. child requirements).
- Estimable: As a single unit, this requirement cannot be estimated because it bundles heterogeneous legal/functional topics (exclusion grounds, professional registers, suitability, financial standing, technical ability) without a gap-analysis or crosswalk between current national criteria and the cited EC articles. This is expected behavior for a policy/epic-tier item and is resolved through decomposition rather than being an inherent defect, but estimation cannot proceed in the current form. Recommendation: Commission a gap-analysis/crosswalk artifact mapping national qualitative selection/exclusion rules to each relevant EC article (after legal citation is confirmed), and decompose into atomic sub-requirements before attempting estimation.
- Small: The requirement spans at least five distinct legal/functional topics across multiple articles, making it epic-sized rather than story-sized. This is a category mismatch typical of policy-tier/root requirements rather than a discovered defect, but it still means the item is not actionable within a single iteration as currently scoped. Recommendation: Decompose into article-level sub-requirements (e.g., REQ_002a-f mapped to exclusion grounds, suitability, financial standing, technical/professional ability) once the legal citation is confirmed, ensuring each sub-item is independently small and sprint-sized.
- Testable: No acceptance criteria, verification method, or test oracle is defined. The term 'correspond' has no specified pass/fail threshold, and no conformance artifact (e.g., ESPD field-mapping ruleset, crosswalk document) exists for an auditor or tester to use. This is a genuine, standing gap independent of the policy-tier framing. Recommendation: Define explicit conformance criteria clarifying 'correspond to' semantics and attach a verification mechanism (legal review sign-off, ESPD schema validation, or audit checklist) once the legal citation and decomposition are finalized.

original_text: Sorting results should take less than 0.1 seconds.
refined_text: When a user re-sorts search results on the video search results page (initial sort, column re-sort, or pagination-triggered sort), the system shall render the newly sorted results client-side (assumed) within 0.1 seconds (p95) (assumed), measured from the user's sort-trigger click to the completed re-render, for result sets of up to 1,000 videos (assumed) on a reference environment of a mid-range desktop browser over a broadband connection (assumed), so that the interaction meets Nielsen's instantaneous-response UX heuristic and sustains user engagement with minimal perceived latency.
findings_used:
- Valuable: While '0.1 seconds' plausibly aligns with Nielsen's instantaneous-response UX heuristic, this linkage is unstated and untraced to any business KPI or user story. This is a moderate documentation gap rather than a complete absence of value, since the number is not arbitrary in industry context. Recommendation: Add explicit traceability to the UX heuristic or business KPI (e.g., engagement, bounce rate) justifying the 0.1s target, ideally framed as 'so that...' outcome value.
- Estimable: Critical information is missing: dataset scale (10 vs 10K vs 1M results), hardware/environment baseline, and whether sorting occurs client-side or server-side. Each factor alone can shift estimation effort by orders of magnitude, making this requirement unsizeable as written. Recommendation: Specify expected dataset size range, reference hardware/network environment, and whether sorting is client-side or server-side before estimation.
- Testable: No measurement methodology (click-to-render vs. API-only), no dataset size for test conditions, no environment specification, and no clarity on hard ceiling vs. percentile basis (p95/p99). These gaps make it impossible to construct a definitive pass/fail test case, and also subsume the unresolved scope ambiguity (initial load vs. re-sort vs. pagination). Recommendation: Define the measurement boundary (trigger-to-render), target dataset size, reference test environment, applicable scenarios (initial sort, re-sort, pagination), and whether the 0.1s target is a hard ceiling or a percentile-based SLA (e.g., p95).

original_text: Our development team must thoroughly investigate each website within our database each month, to ensure that no illegal or harmful content is exposed to our users.
refined_text:
1. Automated pre-indexing scan: When a new website is added to our database, the system shall automatically scan it against an approved content-risk taxonomy (categories: malware, CSAM, piracy, hate speech) (assumed) before it is indexed and exposed to users. The scan shall complete within 24 hours (assumed) of submission, flag any content scoring above a defined confidence threshold of 85% (assumed) for human review, and record the scan result, timestamp, and classification outcome in an audit log retained for 2 years (assumed). Acceptance criteria: 100% of newly added sites have a logged scan result prior to indexing; false-negative rate on a validated test sample ≤2% (assumed).

2. Backlog risk-reduction program for existing sites: The team shall reduce unreviewed high-risk content exposure among the existing site database from its current baseline (to be measured in the first sprint, assumed baseline of 10,000 unreviewed sites) by prioritizing sites via a risk-scoring model (assumed factors: traffic volume, prior complaint history, category sensitivity), reviewing the top 500 highest-risk sites per month (assumed) using a combination of automated scanning and manual review. Acceptance criteria: a monthly report showing number of sites reviewed, number reclassified/actioned, and resulting change in aggregate risk score; target is a 50% reduction (assumed) in the high-risk unreviewed backlog within 6 months (assumed).

3. Confirmed harmful-content incident reduction target: The team shall reduce confirmed incidents of illegal or harmful content exposure to users (as defined by the approved Trust & Safety classification policy, assumed to reference applicable statutory categories such as CSAM, terrorism content, and copyright infringement) by 75% (assumed) relative to the current baseline rate of such confirmed incidents over the trailing 12 months, measured quarterly, with the specific detection method, sampling strategy, and review cadence left to the implementation team's discretion subject to review by Legal/Trust & Safety. Acceptance criteria: quarterly incident report comparing actual confirmed incidents against baseline and target trendline.
findings_used:
- Negotiable: The requirement is phrased as an absolute compliance mandate ('must thoroughly investigate each website... each month... no illegal or harmful content'), using prescriptive modal language and unbounded quantifiers rather than describing a negotiable outcome. This forecloses legitimate implementation choices (risk-based sampling vs. full review, automated+human hybrid vs. manual audit, fixed monthly cadence vs. event-driven scanning). This is a structural failure characteristic of a policy statement, not a negotiable backlog artifact, and compounds the Small/Testable failures rather than being mere 'friction.' Recommendation: Rewrite as an outcome-oriented statement (e.g., 'Reduce exposure of unreviewed high-risk content to near-zero via a combination of automated scanning and prioritized manual review') and explicitly invite the team to propose detection method, sampling strategy, and cadence as implementation details subject to negotiation.
- Valuable: The underlying intent — protecting users from illegal/harmful content — is self-evidently important for trust, safety, and legal/regulatory exposure. However, value is asserted rather than demonstrated: there is no baseline metric, target state, or definition of 'harmful' against which delivered value can be confirmed. For a perpetual, resource-consuming commitment, an unquantified value claim is a genuine prioritization and governance risk, not merely a low-concern nicety. Recommendation: Attach a measurable value statement and baseline (e.g., current incident/exposure rate) plus a target (e.g., reduce confirmed harmful-content exposure incidents by X% or achieve Y% scan coverage within Z hours of site addition) so value delivery can be verified over time, not just asserted at intake.
- Estimable: Effort cannot be sized in any form, not even a rough order-of-magnitude estimate. 'Thoroughly' has no defined depth or method (keyword scan vs. manual review vs. legal sign-off), there is no content-category breakdown (malware, CSAM, piracy, hate speech each carry different effort/risk profiles), and no stated volume of websites exists to apply a unit-cost or time estimate against. This is a blocking defect for sprint planning. Recommendation: Before estimation, obtain: (1) an approved content-risk taxonomy from Legal/Trust & Safety, (2) the current database size/scale, and (3) a defined detection methodology per category. Only then can child stories receive story points or time estimates.
- Small: This reads as an ongoing, unbounded compliance program rather than a sprint-sized deliverable. 'Each website' implies full-population coverage with no segmentation, 'each month' implies perpetual recurring commitment, and 'no illegal or harmful content' is an absolute, unbounded success condition with no MVP slice. Recurrence itself is not disqualifying if the per-cycle unit were bounded (e.g., 'scan newly added sites this month'), but here the population and standard are both unbounded, compounding with the recurring cadence into an epic mislabeled as a single requirement. Recommendation: Decompose by content-risk category and by detection mechanism (automated vs. manual) into bounded, cycle-scoped child stories — e.g., 'Automated scan of newly indexed sites within 24 hours' as one story and a separately throttled, tracked backlog-reduction program for existing sites as another.
- Testable: No acceptance criteria exist in testable form. 'Illegal or harmful' has no reference to statute, policy, or classification system against which a QA engineer could write a test case; 'thoroughly investigate' produces no defined output artifact (log, report, takedown action, dashboard flag); and no pass/fail threshold is given (zero-tolerance vs. acceptable false-negative rate, audit trail requirement). As written, the requirement is unverifiable and no test plan can be derived from it. This also carries legal/audit-defensibility risk given the content domain (e.g., CSAM) if 'thoroughly' is ever challenged without a documented standard. Recommendation: Define measurable, documented acceptance criteria per decomposed story (e.g., false-negative rate ≤ Y%, 100% of new sites scanned pre-indexing, audit log retained for Z days, classification confidence threshold for human review) referencing an approved taxonomy/policy document, and flag the current unbounded wording to Legal/Compliance as an audit-defensibility risk independent of the engineering backlog.

original_text: System shall display the hyperlinks and descriptions for the user to perform the desired functions as specified in the related UIS.
refined_text:
**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-1:** The system shall display, for each of the 8 core functions (assumed: Dashboard, Reports, Settings, Profile, Notifications, Help, Logout, Search), a navigable control (e.g., link, button, or tile) accompanied by a short descriptive label, enabling end-users to discover and access these functions without prior training.

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-2:** For each function control, the system shall determine availability based on the end-user's assigned role. Controls for functions the user is not authorized to use shall be rendered in a visibly disabled state with an explanatory tooltip stating "You do not have permission to access this function" (assumed). Controls for authorized functions shall, upon selection, navigate the user to the corresponding function screen within 2 seconds (assumed).

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_001-3:** All function controls and their descriptive labels shall comply with WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility guidelines (assumed), including providing accessible names for screen readers. If a selected function's target screen fails to load within 5 seconds (assumed), the system shall display the message "This function is temporarily unavailable, please try again later" (assumed) instead of a broken or blank screen.
findings_used:
- Independent: The requirement defers its entire substantive content to an externally referenced 'related UIS' with no document ID, version, or baseline date. While referencing a controlled UIS is a standard and acceptable traceability pattern in structured SDLCs, the lack of version pinning means the requirement's meaning can silently shift if the UIS changes, and its status (draft vs. baselined) is unverified. This is a resolvable, metadata-level gap rather than a fundamental structural flaw. Recommendation: Pin the reference to a specific UIS document ID and version/baseline date, and confirm the UIS is approved/frozen before this requirement is considered ready for implementation.
- Negotiable: The term 'hyperlinks' prescribes a specific UI implementation rather than an outcome, foreclosing alternative navigation patterns (buttons, tiles, menu cards). The requirement also conflates fixed intent (users can discover/access functions) with negotiable form (visual layout, widget type), and largely defers all specifics to the UIS without adding independent negotiable value. Recommendation: Replace implementation-specific terms like 'hyperlinks' with outcome-based language (e.g., 'navigable controls' or 'interactive elements') and explicitly separate fixed intent from negotiable presentation details.
- Valuable: The requirement is phrased purely as system behavior without an articulated user benefit (e.g., discoverability, reduced navigation effort, clarity). While the value (helping users find and access functions) is reasonably inferable from context, it is not explicitly stated, and no persona is identified, leaving the value proposition implicit rather than demonstrated. Recommendation: Add a concise value statement, e.g., 'enabling users to discover and access available functions without prior training,' and identify the target persona(s) (end-user, admin, etc.).
- Estimable: Sizing depends entirely on the number and complexity of 'desired functions' defined in the UIS, which is unknown without inspecting that document. Additional hidden complexity factors (localization, role-based/conditional rendering) are unaddressed. A rough order-of-magnitude estimate may be possible once UIS existence and scope are confirmed, but as written, precise estimation is not currently possible. Recommendation: Confirm UIS availability and scope to produce at least a rough order-of-magnitude estimate; explicitly state whether localization and permission-based rendering are in scope.
- Small: This reads as a parent/epic-level requirement describing a general display behavior across potentially many screens or functions defined in the UIS, rather than a single, independently deliverable slice. 'Display' also bundles multiple concerns (rendering, filtering by permission, dynamic description text, accessibility labeling) that could each be separate stories. Recommendation: Treat this as a parent/epic requirement and decompose it into one child requirement per screen or function group once the UIS content is enumerated.
- Testable: There is no enumerated list of hyperlink labels, descriptions, or target destinations, no acceptance criteria for content accuracy or synchronization with the UIS, and no defined behavior for edge cases (e.g., disabled or unavailable functions) or non-functional constraints (accessibility, broken-link handling). As written, no verifiable pass/fail oracle can be constructed. Recommendation: Add explicit, enumerable acceptance criteria referencing a specific UIS section/table of links and targets, including expected behavior for disabled/unavailable functions and relevant accessibility or non-functional constraints.

original_text: The User shall be able to view the hyperlinks and descriptions listed.
refined_text:
**BLITDRAFT_REQ_002-A:** The system shall display, within the resource list panel, a vertically scrollable list of all hyperlinks and their associated descriptions retrieved from the application's resource repository (assumed), rendered in the DOM and visible without requiring the user to click any additional control. The list shall display up to 20 items per page (assumed) and shall be sorted alphabetically by hyperlink title (assumed), with pagination controls shown when more than 20 items exist.

- Given the resource repository contains one or more entries, when the user navigates to the resource list panel, then each entry's hyperlink text and description shall be rendered and visible on screen within 2 seconds (assumed).
- Given the repository contains more than 20 entries, when the user reaches the end of the current page, then pagination controls shall allow navigation to subsequent pages without full page reload.

**BLITDRAFT_REQ_002-B:** The system shall handle edge cases in the hyperlink/description list as follows:

- Given the resource repository contains no entries, when the user opens the resource list panel, then the system shall display the message "No resources available" (assumed) in place of the list.
- Given a hyperlink entry has a missing or empty description, when the list is rendered, then the system shall display the placeholder text "No description provided" (assumed) instead of leaving the field blank.
- Given a hyperlink is broken or unreachable, when the user clicks it, then the system shall display an inline error message "This link is currently unavailable" (assumed) rather than navigating to an error page.
- Given a description exceeds 150 characters (assumed), when rendered in the list, then the text shall be truncated with an ellipsis and expandable via a "Read more" control (assumed).
findings_used:
- Independent: The term 'listed' lacks a traceable antecedent to a parent requirement defining where the list resides and what data source populates it. Consensus reclassifies this as a traceability/completeness gap rather than a true Independence defect, but it still prevents the requirement from standing alone for implementation or verification. Recommendation: Add an explicit reference/link to the parent requirement or Epic that defines the source and location of the hyperlink/description list before sprint entry.
- Estimable: Key terms are undefined, but these fall into two distinct categories: (1) visual/styling ambiguity (hyperlink appearance, description formatting) which is typically resolved via reference to existing mockups/design system, and (2) functional/behavioral ambiguity (list pagination, sorting, scrolling, empty-state handling) which represents a genuine blocking gap requiring explicit specification. Recommendation: Resolve functional behavior (pagination/scroll/sort/empty-state) via explicit acceptance criteria before estimation; resolve visual/styling details via reference to mockups or design system rather than rewriting the requirement.
- Testable: No acceptance criteria exist, no Given/When/Then scenarios are defined, and 'view' is not operationally defined (rendered in DOM vs. visible without scrolling vs. clickable). Edge cases such as empty list, broken link, missing description, and text overflow are entirely unaddressed. This is the strongest and most defensible blocking finding. Recommendation: Draft explicit Given/When/Then acceptance criteria covering normal display and edge cases (empty list, broken link, missing/truncated description) before this requirement can enter a sprint.
